generation.forced_text:
I remember the way I walked up my favorite street, as though I could walk through its history and know each coble stone that cracked beneath foot or every nock and knot that carved into a doorjamb.

This morning as sunlight filtered in the gap behind clouds, illuminting my front yard as I began walking to my grandmother. My mind wandered back through time - to how it had all looked, the first morning after I came from my birth mother to be in a house like the one before us, my mother in a long night dress in our doorway as the streetlights dimmest. How the smell, that of freshly baked cookies in a brown bag in our car as my mother held it to our face. I was six, maybe even younger and I knew I had come into that world for something special.

Now that house is no where
